newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hopes to clear up Hebron issues on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Israel hopes to clear up Hebron issues on Monday.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said he hoped Israeli and Palestinian negotiators would clear up by late on Monday all issues standing in the way of an elusive Hebron deal.

"We hope that by tomorrow evening we'll find solutions to the subjects that remain in dispute," he told reporters after a 90-minute meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in the self-ruled Gaza Strip.

"We agreed to follow up on all the levels and our negotiating teams and we will continue tomorrow, God willing, for a follow-up in order to solve all of the unsolved problems," Arafat told their joint news conference.

Neither man would give a date but Israeli and PLO officials have said they expect Arafat and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to sign an agreement giving the Palestinians control of 80 percent of Hebron by Tuesday, the end of the year.
Hebron is the last of seven occupied West Bank cities Israel agreed to give self-rule to under an agreement signed with the PLO in 1995. The PLO took over much of the Gaza Strip in 1994.

U.S. President Bill Clinton's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was due back in the region on Monday to mediate any last-minute snags and attend the signing. Security concerns have held up the handover in Hebron, including demands by Netanyahu for additional measures he says are needed to protect the 400 Jewish settlers in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
